text:
Emma: heads up — we pushed the torch.compile + cudagraphs pilot to 70% traffic and are seeing a latency spike on short sequences (seqlen=8). looks like kernel selection flipped during runtime and kv-cache hit-rate dropped. investigating.

Jon: rough numbers? p50/p95 change?

Emma: p50 +0.6ms, p95 +4ms on gen path. token-level profiling shows a ~3.2ms increase per token for short-prefix scenarios. long seqlen workloads unaffected.

Li: interesting. do you have an nvtx / profiler dump? could be cudagraph re-use mismatch causing different kernel variant to be chosen.

Emma: pasted short profiler snippet below (nvprof flavour):

```
-- kernel selection summary --
matmul_sgemm_fused  chosen for shapes (bs=1, H=1024, S=64)  avg 0.12ms
matmul_sgemm_opt_v2 chosen for shapes (bs=1, H=1024, S=8)   avg 0.47ms
copy_kernel_async     called more often for KV buffer moves
cudaMemcpyAsync       increased by 18% (more mem ops)
```

Seems torch.compile + dynamic-shape graph created a slightly different allocation pattern for KV cache (extra padding), which trips our seqlen-bucketing logic into the "small" bucket and the autotuner picks opt_v2 (lower throughput but better for larger S) — but on tiny S it's worse.

Jon: that matches a hypothesis: our autotuner heuristics currently use the raw tensor shape bytes to index kernel candidates. if cudagraphs+jit adds a different stride or alloc offset we might misclassify. can you dump the exact shapes/strides?

Emma: here are the tensor descriptors we logged (bs, seqlen, head_dim, stride):
```
(1,8,128, stride=131072)
(1,64,128, stride=1048576)
(1,8,128, stride=131080)  # note the +8 padding for compiled graph path
```

Li: that +8 is the smoking gun. autotuner hash = f(shape, stride, dtype). small padding makes it a different bucket. we should normalize stride before lookup.

perf-bot: perf CI job queued: https://ci.redwood.ai/ops/12345 — collecting full pprof and kernel timelines.

Jon: aside — why did kv-cache hit-rate drop? padding shouldn't change logical keys.

Emma: our prefix cache key encodes (ptr, offset, len) in a tuple for quick equality, and the ptr changed when cudagraph preallocs with a different offset. so equal logical prefixes now look different -> cache miss -> extra copies -> memcpy overhead -> kernel path gets different batching characteristics.

Li: ugh. two problem vectors: 1) autotuner bucketing uses raw allocation descriptors 2) cache key uses pointer identity. both brittle under JIT/cudagraphs.

Jon: proposed remediation: a) normalize tensor descriptors (zero out alloc offset) before autotuner hash, b) make prefix cache key content-based (hash first 64 bytes) + pointer fallback, c) add a short-circuit in kernel picker to prefer fused matmul for S <= 16 when latency is primary SLO.

Emma: agree. i can prototype (a) and (c) this sprint. (b) needs perf impact analysis — hashing first 64 bytes could be heavy but we can memoize.

Li: for (a) trivial: in runtime/kernel_picker.cpp replace: 
```
key.stride = desc.stride; // old
key.stride = normalize_stride(desc); // new
```
normalize_stride should divide out known cudagraph padding patterns.

Emma: i'll add NVTX ranges and rerun the pilot once PR is up. also adding a quick metric in Console: "kv_cache_miss_rate_by_alloc_pattern" so we can roll back automatically if it exceeds threshold.

infra-bot: rollout paused for the cohort hitting the regression (cohort: experiment/torch-compile-v2). Traffic shifted back to control.

Jon: action items:
- Emma: PR for normalizing descriptor and kernel-picker short-circuit (ETA: EOD Thurs)
- Li: draft change for safe content-hash fallback in cache (ETA: next week)
- Emma + perf-bot: run full perf job and attach pprof + nvprof output to ticket #INF-987

Emma: ok starting on PR. dropping a repro command for anyone who wants to run locally:
```
# repro script (docker image with nvprof)
python -m perf.run_workload --model redwood-7b --batch 1 --seqlen 8 --jit=compile --cudagraphs=true --trace nvtx --output /tmp/prof
```

Jon: thanks. @Li if you can review the autotuner change quickly we can re-enable the pilot behind the feature flag. :thumbsup:

Li: will do. one more note — also monitor kernel occupancy in Console; sometimes the "opt_v2" is higher occupancy and worse for latency at tiny S. adding that chart to per-model dashboard.

Emma: noted. I'll post the PR link when ready.

perf-bot: perf job completed: https://ci.redwood.ai/ops/12345/artifacts/pprof.tar.gz (contains pprof, nvprof timelines, and a small script to reproduce the bucket hash).

Emma: closing loop here — thanks all. we'll track in #INF-987.
